title: RTI Forum asks for a stronger, independent Information Commission
excerpt: Civil society leaders including TIB, BLAST, COAST and Nagorik Uddyog want commissioners given the status of Supreme Court judges, plus staff and a budget.
content:
The Right to Information (RTI) Forum on Tuesday (24 November) called on the government to strengthen the independence, staffing and budget of the Information Commission, The Business Standard reported. A forum delegation met the newly appointed commission the same day and offered technical support.

In a statement, the forum said the commission has powers equal to a civil court under the RTI Act. It can investigate complaints, issue decisions, impose fines and recommend disciplinary action against officials. Because commissioners can be removed on the same grounds as Supreme Court judges, the forum said the chief information commissioner and other commissioners should have the status and pay of Appellate Division and High Court Division judges respectively.

The forum also asked for enough staff, an annual budget for operations and public awareness, and a full-time secretary with RTI experience.

The statement was signed by forum convener Shaheen Anam and core group members including Dr Badiul Alam Majumdar (SHUJAN), Dr Iftekharuzzaman (Transparency International Bangladesh), Rezaul Karim Chowdhury (COAST Trust), Syed Sultan Uddin Ahmmed (BILS), AHM Bazlur Rahman (BNNRC) and Zakir Hossain (Nagorik Uddyog). Barrister Sara Hossain of BLAST was among other signatories.

Why it matters

NGOs, journalists and community groups use RTI requests to check spending on safety nets, health and public works. A commission without staff, funds or status cannot enforce the law against reluctant offices.

What to watch

Whether the government responds on status and budget, and how quickly the new commission clears its complaint backlog.

Sources

  • The Business Standard: Ensure Information Commission's independence, parity for commissioners with SC judges: RTI Forum, 24 November 2026
